title: skill_block holds on Windows: a drive-letter berth is a berth and its proofs read the child's words
intention: skill_block's berth map and its proofs hold on every box: a berth pointer is a berth wherever its path is absolute, and the proofs read what their CLI children say.
why: Measured 2026-11-13 on akiendell under ~/.cairn/venv (Python 3.14): skill_block's proofs run 12 red, 47 green, from three causes. (1) skill_block.py _berth_key (line 462) and _idea_berth (line 473) take a berth pointer as a path only when it starts with '/', so every Windows berth (C:\...) is dropped: berth_ticket_cursors returns {} and the review lane drains nothing; 9 teeth of test_review_lane_drains_by_measurement.py red on it. (2) test_skill_block.py's CLI children write stderr in the console code page (cp1252, where the em-dash is byte 0x97) and the proof decodes utf-8, so the reader thread dies and r.stderr is None: 2 teeth red with TypeError. (3) test_the_wire_is_not_fatal_when_the_ROOTS_are_unwritable locks the root with chmod(0o500), which does not stop a write into a directory on Windows, so a berth is written and printed: 1 tooth red.
traces_to: Law 3 (a green on Linux is not a measurement on Windows); Law 9; the review lane's drain-by-measurement rule (open-d0a5003c404a).
how: D1 _berth_key/_idea_berth accept an absolute path on either platform. D2 the CLI teeth decode utf-8 and give the child PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8. D3 the unwritable-root tooth locks with a file in the way, plus chmod on POSIX. D4 a tooth that the platform's absolute berth is mapped.

clauses.claim: berth_ticket_cursors maps a ticket whose intent_berth is the platform's absolute path or a '/'-rooted path to that berth, and ignores 'none, because ...'
test_cli_fires_and_refuses_with_honest_exit_codes and test_cli_refuses_an_unreadable_packet_by_name are green on Windows with the child's stderr decoded
test_the_wire_is_not_fatal_when_the_ROOTS_are_unwritable, locked by a file where the root's directory must go, sees exit 0, berth None and NO BERTH EXISTS on Windows and Linux

decisions.text: D1: _berth_key and _idea_berth take a pointer as a path when it starts with '/' or Path(v).is_absolute().
D2: test_skill_block.py's CLI subprocesses pass encoding='utf-8', errors='replace' and PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8 in the child env.
D3: the unwritable-root tooth locks the root with a file standing where its directory must go, on every platform, and with chmod(0o500) as a second case on POSIX.
D4: test_review_lane_drains_by_measurement.py gains a tooth that _berth_key keeps a '/'-rooted pointer, keeps the platform's absolute path, and drops 'none, because ...'.

out: the CLI's output encoding to an operator console (its code page is right for it)

measured.how: in-process call over the proof's World() ticket
